result.notes:
The accounts lane is booked: 141 records of its own. That is 7 tables, 4 machines, 44 procedures, 69 rpcs, 6 workflows and 11 flows. They cover all 75 operations registered under packages/backend/convex/accounts/*. The 26 public protocol rows use row-name ids (e.g. accounts.safes.load-by-auth-user-id); internal operations use <concept>.<area>.<file>.

Typecheck: `npx tsc -p books` reports only unresolved imports in my files. The 18 records listed in `missing` are still absent (vocabulary events, the parties and profiles procedures, activity/overlays, permissions/commands). These imports already resolve against sibling lanes: access, organizations, permissions, payments, payroll, requests and operator procedures/rpcs; the external.ts contracts (agent-owner, test-money-token, companies-house-claimer, safe); and the chain-rpc calls.

Every accounts record that payments/neighbors.ts stood in is defined with the same id and export name:
- tables: accounts, smart-accounts, approvals
- procedures: account-id-for-auth-user-or-null, require-account-signer-in-tx, require-payment-account-in-tx, read-accounts-at-safe-in-tx, find-account-recipient-in-tx, resolve-account-recipient-safe-in-tx, read-execution-approval-in-tx

Every name other lanes import from ../accounts/* exists.

I ran the book build in a scratch copy with stubs for the missing modules. All records decode. The only accounts problems were dangling links to those stubs, plus 49 call-error-not-declared hits on accounts.summaries.home and accounts.grants.mint-welcome-grant. Those hits are left on purpose: both catch and absorb their chain failures, so a caller never receives those codes.

Judgments:
1. Seven action-side door exports are booked as procedures because siblings link them: withServiceLane, mintTestTokens, mintTestTokensOnce, mintBankDepositTokens, relayOpenCalls, readPositions, readTokenBalances. Their chain calls are described in the about text, since a procedure has no calls field. faucetSafeAddressForSigner and withChain are pure helpers and not booked.
2. Convex `.unique()` reads list UNKNOWN, because a duplicate row throws a plain Error.
3. smart-accounts has a lifecycle but no state column, so it is described on the table, not booked as a machine. The agent machine covers only the stored state (creating, active, failed). Frozen and removed are derived from flags and described in the about text.
4. The three event posters (emit-safe-confirmed, emit-member-activation, emit-transitioned) are rpcs whose about starts with "Telemetry plumbing:".
5. The workflows are send-approved, expire, notify, mint-welcome-grants, follow and follow-change. mint-welcome-grant, send-signed and send-change-signed are rpcs, because a workflow runs them through ctx.runAction rather than scheduling them.
6. A trigger names one rpc, but some workflows have more starters. expire and notify name accounts.approvals.request, though every open schedules them; mint-welcome-grants names provision, though Organizations' setup also schedules it. The other starters are said in the about text.
7. Other concepts' operations an action runs are named in the about text, and their tables are not folded in, which would make false write-boundary findings. These are organizations.treasuries.load, payroll.runs.list, activity.items.list, parties.recipients.resolve, the relayed sendSigned actions and payments.executions.complete.
8. Approvals reads Payments' moneyExecutions table directly (consume-approved, reschedule-approved, send-approved). It is booked as a read: a boundary finding.
9. Three codes that cross as defects keeping their own code are declared: ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED and PROVIDER_RESPONSE_INVALID on faucet-mint, ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED on agents.create.
10. reads.ts defines no records: the old reads/ folder registers no operation, and its door functions are in procedures.ts.
11. flows.ts re-exports flow_client_approvals_prepare from payments/flows.ts. It books flows only for SDK methods with several calls or real local work; one-rpc forwarders are listed in its closing comment.
12. client.holdings.current has `calls: []`. The SDK's own Ponder reader has no integration record (external.ts says it is not the backend reader). This is a gap.
13. Spans are `chain.read <method>` per chain-rpc request, and SDK spans only where runCapxulEffect or runPortEffect opens one. Workflow timeoutMs is 600000, the Convex action limit, as payments does it.

Findings recorded in the about text:
- The SDK's isRelayed omits `agent`. reject therefore asks Payments to abandon an execution that does not exist, and submit sends agent approvals to submitCommand.
- recordApproval ignores its `now` argument.
- recordDeployment clears the claim lock's lease stamp (deploymentInFlightAt) but leaves claimLockId.
- readWorkspaceSetupSignerInTx's deployedAt check always passes.
- agents.list shows lapsed creates as creating.
- The agents by_safe_address index has no query.
- readAccountOwnerInTx and readWorkspaceViewerSafeInTx have no callers.
- getLifecycle needs a successful chain balance read before it reports ready.
- depositInstructions always says base-sepolia.
- The README's operation table is stale.

Nothing is committed.
